subject: POC rate realignment and safety-net authorization
messages:
From: Jordan Price <jordan.price@novamed.io>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@novamed.io>, finance@novamed.io
Date: Sun, 8 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: POC rate realignment + safety-net for usage spike

Hi Mateo,

Thanks again for the quick demo last week. Our engineering team started the initial POC yesterday and we’re seeing two things: (1) the token profile is spikier than we estimated (short bursts of high QPS for model evals), and (2) the early telemetry suggests we’ll exceed the starter rate band by ~2.5x over the first 30 days.

Pricing at the current committed starter tier will blow out our budget for this POC. Would Redwood consider a temporary realignment for the POC period (30 days) to the interim tier you mentioned on the call, and include a safety-net cap so we don’t incur runaway overages if usage spikes again during load tests? We want to move fast but need predictability.

Attached is a short usage extract and the initial scope for the POC. We can sign a short addendum or DocuSign if needed.

What we need from Redwood:
- A temporary rate for the POC (30 days) aligned to the medium-tier unit price we discussed
- A safety-net cap (monthly ceiling) and an agreed rollback to normal pricing after 30 days
- Confirmation of any minimum commitment or invoice timing changes

Can you confirm next steps? We’re aiming to start extended load tests on Nov 12.

Thanks,
Jordan
Account Lead, NovaMed
Jordan.Price@novamed.io
+1 (415) 555-0199

Attachments: nova_poc_pricing_sheet_v4.xlsx
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Price <jordan.price@novamed.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 8 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: POC rate realignment + safety-net for usage spike

Jordan — thanks for the context and the file. I pulled the initial telemetry and put together a short recommendation; attaching a one-pager and a proposed 30-day addendum.

Short answer: we can provide an interim rate and a safety-net cap for the POC, but this requires a VP/CFO signoff because it sits outside our standard starter-tier guardrails. The commercial ask is: a temporary unit price aligned to the medium tier, a hard usage ceiling of $18k for the month, and automatic rollback to the originally quoted starter rates at day 31 unless NovaMed opts into a committed tier.

Key tradeoffs I highlighted for exec review:
- Revenue impact vs. conversion probability (this is a pre-commitment conversion motion; we estimate a ~35% chance of expansion if POC meets success criteria)
- Operational risk if load tests spike beyond the safety-net (we recommend a hard cap + real-time alerting and optional throttling)
- Billing and timing: invoice net30 for any consumption above the monthly cap to avoid cashflow friction for the customer

Marcus and Marissa — I’m looping you in to confirm numbers and ask for the exec approval path. I’ve attached the draft addendum (nova_poc_pricing_sheet_v4.xlsx) and a brief risk mitigation doc.

Next steps: can Marissa propose precise wording for the executive memo? We’ll need a short business case and recommended signoff language for VP/CFO.

— Mateo
Sr. Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 09:07:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: Request: POC rate realignment + safety-net for usage spike

On Mon, Nov 8, 2026 at 11:05 AM Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com> wrote:
> Marcus and Marissa — I’m looping you in to confirm numbers and ask for the exec approval path. I’ve attached the draft addendum (nova_poc_pricing_sheet_v4.xlsx) and a brief risk mitigation doc.

Thanks Mateo — reviewed the telemetry and the draft. My recommended commercial exception is below. This is written for VP/CFO sign-off language.

Recommendation (compact):
- Grant a 30-day POC rate realignment to NovaMed at the interim medium-tier unit price (as in attached sheet).
- Implement a hard safety-net cap of $18,000 for the 30-day period; any usage beyond cap will be paused and billed per agreed overage terms after manual review.
- Require NovaMed to sign the short addendum (DocuSign link) before the extended load tests start on Nov 12.
- If NovaMed converts to a committed tier within 90 days, apply an onramp credit of up to $6,000 to offset the temporary concession (credit applied to first invoice after conversion).

Business case summary for signoff:
- Upside: High conversion likelihood — team estimate 30–40% expansion within 3 months if POC is successful.
- Downside: Short-term margin erosion capped by hard ceiling; minimal operational exposure with throttling + alerting.
- Controls: Require pre-sign of addendum; finance to set invoice net30; sales to monitor daily consumption and notify revenue ops at 75% of cap.

Attachments: risk_mitigation_plan.pdf (outlines throttling and alert thresholds).

Signoff ask for VP/CFO:
"Approve a one-time, timeboxed pricing realignment and $18k safety-net for NovaMed POC (Deal ND-2026-0781). Authorization contingent on signed addendum and implementation of throttling/alerting controls."

If Marcus agrees on the numbers I think this is ready to route to Karthik for approval.

— Marissa Cole
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 16:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: POC rate realignment + safety-net for usage spike

Thanks for the clear memo and the controls. I approve the one-time, timeboxed concession with these conditions:

1) $18,000 hard safety-net cap is approved for the 30-day POC window (Nov 12 — Dec 11).
2) Addendum must be signed by NovaMed before Nov 12 and include explicit rollback language on day 31.
3) Revenue Ops to create a dedicated invoice code so we can track concession impact; apply up to $6,000 onramp credit only if NovaMed executes a 12-month committed tier within 90 days.
4) Product/Infra (Marcus) to enable the throttling + alerting thresholds and confirm they are operational before Nov 12.
5) Sales to notify finance at 75% utilization of cap and again at 100% (automatic pause if 100% hit unless Marcus confirms throttling override).

Marcus — please confirm readiness and post a short note when throttling/alerts are live. Mateo/Marissa — route the addendum to DocuSign and confirm once signed; Finance will generate the dedicated invoice code (ND-2026-0781-AD).

Karthik
VP, Finance & Commercial Strategy
Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com
